jurisdiction.name: Malta
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Malta implements the EU AI Act through legal notices issued in October 2025: the Artificial Intelligence Regulations make the Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) the main market surveillance, notifying and sandbox authority, with penalties applying from August 2026, and a separate notice designates the data protection commissioner (IDPC) for law-enforcement, border and justice high-risk AI. National policy rests on the 2019 national AI strategy, being realigned for 2025-2030 after a public consultation that closed in February 2026, and the 2019 Ethical AI Framework with voluntary AI certification under the MDIA.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The laws were read on the official legislation portal, but the main government, digital authority and financial regulator websites blocked access, so the strategy documents could only be located and some guidance is listed as leads.

instruments.summary: Public consultation (gov.mt reference NL-0040-2025) on a realigned National AI Strategy and Vision replacing the 2019 strategy. According to the MDIA's page on the realignment, it moves from a technology-first approach to one centred on societal well-being and sustainability, organised around two enablers, three growth pillars (data and infrastructure, leveraging AI, advancing AI) and five foundational principles, with 83 short- to medium-term measures.

instruments.summary: Malta's ethical AI framework, a component of the 2019 national AI strategy. It sets four objectives (human-centric approach; respect for law, human rights and democratic values; maximising benefits while minimising risks; alignment with international norms), guiding principles drawn from the EU High-Level Expert Group (human autonomy, prevention of harm, fairness, explicability) and trustworthy-AI requirements, and is the basis for MDIA's voluntary AI certification by MDIA-approved system auditors.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI ethics framework; basis of the voluntary AI certification programme.

instruments.summary: Malta's first national AI strategy, aiming to make Malta 'the ultimate AI launchpad'. It rests on three strategic pillars (investment, start-ups and innovation; public-sector adoption; private-sector adoption) and three enablers (education and workforce; legal and ethical framework; ecosystem infrastructure), with a short-term action plan of 72 actions incl. six public-sector AI pilot projects and a national AI certification programme.

instruments.issuing_authority: Minister responsible for the Malta Digital Innovation Authority, on the advice of the MDIA (under article 58 of the Malta Digital Innovation Authority Act, Cap. 591)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Government Gazette of Malta No. 21,519 on 10 October 2025 (legal notice dated 7 October 2025 in the portal metadata). Regulation 1(3): regulations 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 (notifying authority, sandbox, penalties and related provisions) come into force on 2 August 2026; the remaining regulations (incl. the designation of the MDIA in reg. 3) have no separate commencement date and so apply from publication. Made in English only (Cap. 591 art. 58(7)).
instruments.summary: Subsidiary legislation (S.L. 591.05) implementing the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) in Malta. It designates the Malta Digital Innovation Authority as market surveillance authority (default authority where no other is designated), single point of contact, notifying authority and sole national authority for the AI regulatory sandbox, with coordination duties with the MFSA for high-risk AI used by financial institutions and with sectoral authorities for Annex I products. It sets administrative penalties of up to EUR 350,000 per infringement or 1% of worldwide turnover for undertakings, with daily penalties and special rules for public authorities.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Malta's main national AI Act implementing measure: designates the AI authorities, the AI regulatory sandbox and the national penalty regime.

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence (Designation of the Information and Data Protection Commissioner for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Regulations, 2025
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence (Designation of the Information and Data Protection Commissioner for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Regulations, 2025 (L.N. 227 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister responsible for data protection, after consultation with the Information and Data Protection Commissioner (under article 33 of the Data Protection Act, Cap. 586)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Government Gazette of Malta No. 21,519 on 10 October 2025. Regulation 1(3): regulations 5 to 7 and 9 to 12 come into force on 2 August 2026; the designation (reg. 3) applies from publication. The IDPC's own page (13 October 2025) confirms publication on 10 October 2025.
instruments.summary: Regulations under the Data Protection Act implementing the EU AI Act that designate the Information and Data Protection Commissioner as market surveillance authority for specified Annex III high-risk AI systems: biometric systems used for law enforcement, border management and justice and democracy, emergency-call evaluation and dispatch and patient triage systems, and law-enforcement AI systems. They give the Commissioner tasks on prohibited AI practices in these areas, set out its role as personal-data supervisory authority alongside the AI Act, and provide for notifications and administrative penalties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Allocates AI Act enforcement over law-enforcement, border and justice high-risk AI to the data protection authority.

instruments.summary: Order adding the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) as item (68) of the Schedule to the Representative Actions (Consumers) Act. Infringements of the AI Act that harm consumers' collective interests can therefore be pursued through representative actions by qualified entities in Malta.

instruments.english_title: Malta Digital Innovation Authority Act (Chapter 591 of the Laws of Malta)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Malta (Act XXXI of 2018, as amended by Act XIX of 2024)
instruments.current_status: In force. Act XXXI of 2018 (dated 15 July 2018 in the consolidated text; portal metadata 6 August 2018), substantially amended by Act XIX of 2024 (consolidated version of 14 June 2024), which also repealed the Innovative Technology Arrangements and Services Act (Cap. 592) under which MDIA's 2019 AI-ITA certification was organised.
instruments.summary: Act establishing the Malta Digital Innovation Authority to promote and regulate innovative technology; its First Schedule (as substituted by Act XIX of 2024) lists artificial intelligence, distributed ledger technology and the internet of things as innovative technology. It sets guiding principles incl. ethical standards in technology development, the Authority's functions, an ethics committee on the use of innovative technologies, enforcement powers and an administrative review tribunal, and empowers the Minister to make regulations (the basis of L.N. 226 of 2025).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding statute of Malta's AI authority and legal basis of the AI Act implementing regulations.

instruments.english_title: Data Protection Act (Chapter 586 of the Laws of Malta)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Malta (Act XX of 2018, as amended by Act XII of 2021 and Legal Notice 212 of 2023)
instruments.current_status: In force since 28 May 2018 (date in the consolidated text); consolidated version of 19 September 2023. It contains no AI-specific provisions; automated decision-making rules come from the GDPR itself.
instruments.summary: Act implementing and further specifying the GDPR in Malta, which governs the processing of personal data by AI systems, including automated processing. It establishes the Information and Data Protection Commissioner, its powers, administrative fines and appeals, and empowers the Minister to make regulations (article 33), the basis of L.N. 227 of 2025 designating the Commissioner under the AI Act.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that applies to AI training and use; legal basis of the IDPC's AI Act role.

organizations.name: Malta Digital Innovation Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: Statutory authority under the Malta Digital Innovation Authority Act (Cap. 591), whose First Schedule lists artificial intelligence as an innovative technology. Owner of the national AI strategy (2019 and its 2025 realignment) and the Ethical AI Framework; designated by L.N. 226 of 2025 as Malta's main AI Act market surveillance authority, single point of contact, notifying authority and sole authority for the national AI regulatory sandbox.
